html:
The Mari, once called Cheremis, are a Finno-Ugric people of the middle Volga, north of today's Kazan. They are on the map for 800.

They lived by farming, hunting, beekeeping and fishing in the forests along the Volga. Their southern neighbours, the Volga Bulgars, traded with them and took tribute. Later they came under the Golden Horde and the Khanate of Kazan. After Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in 1552 they became subjects of Russia, and they rose against it several times. Many Mari kept their old nature religion, with prayers in sacred groves, which is still practised today.
